title: Short Stuff: The O.K. Corral
summary: Short Stuff episode on the gunfight at the O.K. Corral (Tombstone, Arizona, October 26, 1881). The hosts cover the Earp brothers (Wyatt, Virgil, Morgan) as lawmen and their history of enforcing the law selectively, Doc Holliday as their friend, and the Clanton gang and McLaury brothers as the cowboys. They describe the town-leader push for law enforcement, Wyatt Earp's alleged deal offer to Ike Clanton, the pistol whipping earlier that day, the roughly thirty-second gunfight in a vacant lot behind the corral around three o'clock, the casualties, Addie Borland's testimony, the inquest by Justice of the Peace Spicer that found the lawmen acted within their rights, and the later killing of Morgan Earp and Clanton's death.

segments.title: Opening banter and setup
segments.summary: Hosts open the short episode with playful banter about the Wild West, then introduce the gunfight at the O.K. Corral as the topic and note that the popular simplified view of Earps as good guys and cowboys as bad guys needs nuance.

segments.title: The Earps and Doc Holliday
segments.summary: Hosts describe Wyatt Earp's past, including an alleged horse-theft record in California and his time as marshal in Wichita before being run out for corruption. He then joined brother Virgil in Tombstone with brother Morgan as deputies, enforcing the law selectively. Doc Holliday, a dentist from Griffin and skilled gunman, was their friend.

segments.title: The Clanton gang and Tombstone's silver boom
segments.summary: The Clanton gang, including Billy Claiborne, Billy Clanton, and Frank and Tom McLaury, are described as men from wealthy ranching families. The two groups disliked each other for a year as Tombstone grew during a silver boom, and town leaders asked for law enforcement, backing the Earps.

segments.title: Wyatt's deal offer and motive
segments.summary: Hosts say Wyatt Earp wanted to become sheriff of a neighboring county and offered Ike Clanton a deal to turn on his gang, which Ike considered but did not take. Wyatt then reportedly decided Ike's evidence had to be eliminated, and the Earps were said to be spoiling for a fight.

segments.title: The gunfight itself
segments.summary: Hosts describe the gun ban in Tombstone, Virgil Earp's attempt to disarm the cowboys, and earlier pistol whippings that day. The shootout lasted about thirty seconds, with thirty to forty shots fired at close range around three in the afternoon, in a vacant lot behind the corral rather than the corral itself. Three cowboys died, including Billy Clanton and both McLaury brothers, while Wyatt was unhurt, Virgil was wounded in the leg, and Morgan was shot through the shoulder area.

segments.title: Inquest, testimony and aftermath
segments.summary: Ike Clanton formally accused the Earps of murder, and eyewitness Addie Borland said people were firing on both sides. Historians think the Earps ordered surrender and fired before the cowboys could drop their weapons. Justice of the Peace Spicer ruled the lawmen acted within their rights. Later, Morgan Earp was murdered in a billiard club in early 1882, Virgil was wounded in an assassination attempt, Ike Clanton was killed in 1887 in Arizona Territory, and Wyatt Earp died at eighty in Los Angeles.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Hosts close the Short Stuff episode with a brief mention of listener contact and show credits.
